pres.title: The Revolving Door: Relapse, Nonadherence and Violence in Schizophrenia
pres.oneliner: Mr. A, a 29-year-old man with schizophrenia, ill since 2014, on his 9th admission, 8 of 9 admissions following nonadherence to olanzapine, with heavy alcohol and heavy tobacco use and past methamphetamine use, admitted for psychosis with aggression.
pres.ddx:
Schizoaffective disorder | Recurrent psychosis with relapses | No mood episodes for a majority of the illness (Criterion D of schizophrenia met)
Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features | Aggression and agitation during relapses | No distinct manic episodes with decreased need for sleep and elevated mood
Methamphetamine-induced psychotic disorder | History of methamphetamine use | Psychosis recurs years after stopping and persists beyond 1 month of abstinence
Alcohol-induced psychotic disorder | Heavy drinking | Psychosis is not confined to intoxication or withdrawal
Psychotic disorder due to another medical condition | Must be excluded | No neurological signs; normal workup

grid.Predisposing|Biological: Family history of psychiatric illness (if present); Methamphetamine use in adolescence; Male sex, early-adult onset
grid.Precipitating|Biological: Stopping olanzapine before admission; Heavy drinking; Resuming smoking, which lowers olanzapine levels (CYP1A2 induction)
grid.Perpetuating|Biological: Recurrent nonadherence; oral regimen; Ongoing alcohol use disorder; Tobacco use disorder; Medication side effects (weight gain, sedation)
grid.Protective|Biological: Clear response to olanzapine when taken; no major medical illness
grid.Predisposing|Psychological: Premorbid personality traits; early adversity (if present)
grid.Precipitating|Psychological: Belief that he no longer needs medication
grid.Perpetuating|Psychological: Poor insight into illness; low motivation; cognitive impairment
grid.Protective|Psychological: Recognizes some early warning signs when well (if present)
grid.Predisposing|Socio-cultural: Low educational or occupational attainment; stigma
grid.Precipitating|Socio-cultural: Conflict at home; loss of supervision of medication
grid.Perpetuating|Socio-cultural: Cost and access to medicines; limited follow-up; peers who drink or smoke
grid.Protective|Socio-cultural: Involved family; access to a mental health service
grid.Protective|Spiritual: Religious community and faith as support (if present)

pres.prognosis:
Good prognostic factors: Clear response to olanzapine; Family involvement; Acute onset of relapses with full remission between episodes (if true).
Poor prognostic factors: 9 readmissions; Repeated nonadherence and poor insight; Comorbid substance use; Violence when unwell; Male sex, early onset.
pres.goalsImm:
Ensure safety of patient and others; manage aggression with the least restrictive measures
Prevent and monitor alcohol withdrawal (CIWA-Ar), give thiamine
Resume antipsychotic treatment and reduce psychotic symptoms
pres.goalsShort:
Achieve remission of positive symptoms
Start a long-acting injectable antipsychotic before discharge
Psychoeducation for patient and family on relapse signs
Begin treatment of heavy alcohol and heavy tobacco use
pres.goalsLong:
Prevent relapse and readmission
Sustain adherence and abstinence
Restore social and occupational functioning
Monitor metabolic health
pres.plans:
Long-acting injectable antipsychotic: olanzapine (subcutaneous monthly Weltruza if available, or IM pamoate with 3-hour observation), or paliperidone, aripiprazole, haloperidol or fluphenazine decanoate depending on access and cost.
Confirm adherence (plasma level or LAI) before calling the illness treatment-resistant; clozapine if two adequate confirmed trials fail.
Treat tobacco use disorder (varenicline or combination NRT); adjust olanzapine if smoking stops or restarts.
Alcohol use disorder: naltrexone or acamprosate with integrated psychosocial treatment; avoid disulfiram.
Metabolic monitoring (APA 2020): weight or BMI every visit for 6 months then quarterly; waist and blood pressure; fasting glucose or HbA1c and lipids at baseline, 4 months, then yearly.
Urine drug screen this admission.
Family psychoeducation; crisis and relapse-prevention plan; close follow-up within 7 days of discharge; consider assertive community treatment.
